messages:
alex: Hey team — multiple customers on dedicated-eu just hit 400s for function calls to our payment-tool integration. Started ~09:12Z, spike ~09:14Z. sample req id: req_0a7f3c. Error: schema_validation_error: missing required field \"action\" in args[0]

maria: Thanks Alex. Can you paste the raw body you sent (redact tokens)? also which model and runtime?

alex: Payload (redacted):
```json
{
  \"tool\": \"payment_tool_v2\",
  \"args\": [{
    \"order_id\": \"ord_12345\",
    \"amount\": 1200
    // NOTE: no \"action\" field here, calling from client as before
  }]
}
```
Using model: redwood-open-34k, runtime: hosted-eu-02

simon: Hmm. The schema for payment_tool_v2 now requires action (capture|authorize) in args[0]. Did we just push a schema change to the model-tool registry or is the runtime using a different tool descriptor?

maria: @simon can you check the registry and recent deploys? I asked the customer for full request-id and logs. They sent:
```
2026-03-17T09:13:47Z ERROR toolcall schema_validation_error req=req_0a7f3c user=acct_998 action=missing_field path=args[0].action
stack: validation->validate_args->raise
```

support-bot: New support ticket created: #TCK-2241 (linked), incident-level: high, affected-customers: 3

katie: I see a release at 09:10Z that updated payment_tool_v2 schema in the catalog (PR #4582). It added required field \"action\" to distinguish capture vs authorize. Looks like backward-incompatible change.

alex: The customers say their client code didn't change and relied on previous lax schema. This caused immediate 400s and a degraded checkout flow. One customer lost ~40 transactions in 8 minutes.

simon: Short-term mitigation: we can rollout a compatibility shim that treats missing action as \"capture\" for backward compatibility until customers migrate. I'll open a quick patch to the registry and deploy a hotfix.

maria: Can you also give steps for customers to patch? We should provide a repro and a direct rollback option.

simon: Repro steps for eng:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/call -H \"Authorization: Bearer <KEY>\" -d '{\"tool\":\"payment_tool_v2\",\"args\":[{\"order_id\":\"ord_12345\",\"amount\":1200}]}'
2) Observe 400 with schema_validation_error and path args[0].action
3) After registry shim, same request returns 200 with tool output JSON including \"status\":\"ok\" and inferred action=\"capture\"

maria: Alex — sent update to affected customers: asked them to implement explicit \"action\" field and provided temporary fallback instructions. Also offered to enable the shim per-customer if they can't deploy quickly.

alex: Customer accepted \"shim-enable\" for their pool and requested ETA. Any estimate?

simon: I can push registry patch and rollout compatibility rules to hosted-eu-02 in ~18 minutes if no blockers. Will post deploy id and trace.

maria: Thanks. Also tagging product and policy: @katie please capture this as a schema-compatibility incident and add to postmortem template. We need guardrails for requiring a migration window on schema bumps.

simon: Deploy id: deploy_20260317_0912_patch, trace: trace_77b2fa. Rolling to 10% then 100% if green. Starting now.

support-bot: Deploy event: deploy_20260317_0912_patch succeeded at 09:28Z for hosted-eu-02 (10% -> 100%).

alex: Post-deploy check: all three affected customers report success, no more 400s. They've resumed checkout flows. Thank you.

maria: We'll keep this thread open for postmortem. Next steps: customer communication summary, timeline, and a template for safe schema changes.

simon: Adding notes to incident board. I'll prepare a minimal test that fails on missing required args for future CI.

alex: closing for now but leave ticket open until PMP complete. :thumbsup:
